description.text: Founded in 1999, The Ensign Group, Inc. (Ensign) is a holding company with independent subsidiaries that provide skilled nursing, senior living and rehabilitative services, as well as other ancillary businesses (including mobile diagnostics and medical transportation), in 17 states. As part of our investment strategy, we also acquire, lease and own healthcare real estate to service the post-acute care continuum through acquisition and investment opportunities in healthcare properties. For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated approximately 95.6% of our revenue from our skilled nursing facilities. The remainder of our revenue is primarily generated from our real estate properties, senior living services and other ancillary services.

analysis_md:
# ENSG — The Ensign Group, Inc.
Engine 5.5 run, 2026-10-19. Market cap $10.19B at $173.05 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B. SIC 8051, skilled nursing care facilities.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, or ttm.json — none are recomputed. Filing figures quoted for the capex override and the litigation item are cited to the FY2025 10-K.

## What it is
The largest US skilled-nursing roll-up: independent operating subsidiaries run skilled nursing, senior living and rehabilitative facilities (373 facilities at FY2025 year-end, 17 states, ~37,900 skilled beds), mostly bought distressed and turned around by local leaders under a decentralized model. A captive REIT, Standard Bearer, owns the real estate (158 owned properties at year-end, 120 operated by Ensign affiliates, the rest leased to third parties under triple-net leases). Revenue is overwhelmingly Medicare/Medicaid/managed-care reimbursement — the government sets the price.

## Owner's earnings
Two definitions, FY2025 (financials_history.csv via EDGAR, capex by override — see OVERRIDE):
- **Conservative (OCF − capex − SBC): latest FY OE/share $5.48** (dcf_numbers.json base_oe_latest_per_share). OCF $564,270,000; SBC $48,299,000; capex $193,557,000 by filing override.
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): printed in the CSV alongside; the OCF-based conservative figure is the one used throughout, because FY2023–24 earnings carry litigation accruals and working-capital swings that the cash series handles more honestly.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Balance sheet (latest FY, CSV/dcf_numbers.json): net debt −$362,125,000 — net cash against funded debt — but that excludes $2,064,029,000 of operating lease liabilities; Ensign leased 253 of its facilities at year-end and bears rent in cost of services ($239,312,000 of rent-cost of services in FY2025 per the 10-K highlights), so the lease load is already inside OE while the funded-debt load is trivial.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct):**
- OCF: FY $564,270,000 − prior YTD $227,950,000 + current YTD $272,108,000 = **TTM $608,428,000**
- Capex: **TTM $193,557,000** — all three legs filled by the filing override, prorated by days (both YTD legs $95,983,060; they cancel, leaving the FY figure)
- SBC: FY $48,299,000 − prior YTD $22,386,000 + current YTD $30,061,000 = **TTM $55,974,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **59,527,000**
- **TTM OE total $358,897,000 → base OE/share $6.03** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $2.66/share — rejected as the base; see BASE_DIVERGENCE under Flags. It is still reported in key_numbers.md and used in the override-impact measurement.

Current prints behind the TTM base: Q2 2026 revenue $1.43B, +17.3% YoY, GAAP diluted EPS $1.68 (company release, July 27, 2026; revenue level and growth per fundamentals.json); management raised FY2026 guidance to revenue $5.87–$5.92B and adjusted EPS $7.75–$7.85. Revenue is not decelerating — TTM revenue YoY is +18.9% (fundamentals.json) against the FY2025 pace of +18.8%, and the Q2 revenue print (+17.3%) sits right on the base start — but cash conversion is: Q2 operating cash flow grew only +10.4% YoY against +17.3% revenue (fundamentals.json). The scenario starts are set against exactly that tension.

## OVERRIDE — capex (filing)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:capex` — Ensign files no capex under any candidate tag from FY2020 onward (the last filed value is FY2019, $71,541,000), so v5 correctly emitted no tier on zero-filled capex.
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 193557000, kind: "filing", source: "Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Purchase of property and equipment': $(193,557) thousand for FY2025, $(158,240) thousand for FY2024 and $(106,180) thousand for FY2023 (statement in thousands)"}`. The override fills only periods with no filed value (FY2020–FY2025 in the annual history; all three TTM legs in ttm.py); filed values are never replaced.
- **Direction of the distortion:** a single value must stand in for six years, and the value chosen is the latest and largest year. Charged against FY2023 (actual filed-statement capex $106,180,000) and FY2024 ($158,240,000) it overstates those years' capex, so it understates the median base — conservative. The same $193.6M against FY2025 is the filer's own exact figure, and management budgets ~$190M of renovation capex for 2026 (FY2025 10-K MD&A), so the TTM leg is at the right level, not padded.
- **Measured impact (key_numbers.md, same final configuration with overrides toggled off):** on the TTM base actually used, base OE/share $9.28 without the override → $6.03 with it (−35.04%); weighted IRR 12.90% → 9.62% (−3.28pp). Unblocks tier: YES — without it the filing gap blocks scoring entirely. The impact is large because the no-override comparison zero-fills capex, which is exactly the fiction v5 exists to refuse.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate; a real operating system, no pricing power
Evidence first (fundamentals.json, filing-direct): ROIC proxy 25.1% / 21.8% / 21.3% / 17.4% / 18.2% / 17.2% for FY2020–FY2025 — well above the cost of capital through a full reimbursement and labor cycle, but drifting down as the portfolio scales. Gross margin slid the other way: 23.1% (FY2021) to 20.1% (FY2025) — labor inflation is winning a point or so a year against fixed reimbursement. A 6, not a 7+: the returns say the turnaround system is real; the payor structure says Ensign can never price its way out of a cost squeeze.
- FOR: turnaround playbook replicated for 26 years — CMS data published Feb 2026 shows same-store survey results 24% better than state peers and a 19% advantage in 4–5-star buildings, most of which were 1–2-star at acquisition; ROIC 17–25% every year FY2020–FY2025; decentralized local-leader model with cluster density (373 facilities, 17 states) and shared Service Center overhead; Standard Bearer captive REIT (158 owned properties) adds cost control and a rent stream; demographic demand tailwind.
- AGAINST: no pricing power — Medicare/Medicaid set the rates; labor is the product and the cost, regulated and scarce; the June 2026 Hunterbrook ("Ensign: The Nursing Home Empire Built on Fatal Neglect", June 8, 2026) and Muddy Waters (June 11, 2026 — administrator licenses allegedly rented at an estimated ~20% of facilities) reports allege part of the margin is understaffing and data gaming — unadjudicated, but they attack the durability of the cost advantage itself, and a securities class action followed (Perusek v. The Ensign Group, C.D. Cal., lead-plaintiff deadline Dec 7, 2026); no switching costs for patients, referrers or staff; growth is substantially bought (102 operations added since 2024); repeat False Claims Act history ($48M settlement in 2013; the 2023 relator settlement below).
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.5 final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended start is 17.45% (rev CAGR 5y 16.08%, 3y 18.48%, latest YoY 18.75%, OE/share CAGR 2y 43.51% — the last is an artifact of the single-value capex override charging FY2025 capex against FY2023, and of the FY2024 OCF trough; the blend's median structure keeps it out of the start). 17.45% sits right on FY2026 guidance (revenue midpoint implies ~+17% on the engine's revenue series; adjusted EPS guidance +18.7% over FY2025), so the base start is guidance, not hope. Scenario starts were set with offsets −0.14 / −0.07 / 0 / +0.03 / +0.08: bear at 10.45% is the Q2 2026 cash-conversion print made permanent — OCF +10.4% YoY while revenue grew +17.3% (fundamentals.json); OE is a cash measure, so the bear case keys off conversion stalling at its latest print even as revenue tracks guidance; bull at 20.45% is modestly above guidance — justified only by the accelerating acquisition pace (20 operations added in Q2 2026 alone, 102 since 2024) and still-rising occupancy, and deliberately trimmed from the +5pp default, which would have started the bull above every print the company has made. Super bull at 25.45% is a stretch case and is weighted as one. Probabilities were shifted left (15/25/30/20/10 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) and the super-bear OE multiplier cut to 0.65, for one named reason: the June 2026 allegations describe a staffing-cost structure that, if regulators force it closed, removes a large slice of OE at a stroke (Hunterbrook's staffing-gap estimate is of the same order as a third of TTM OE) — that is a discrete left tail, not ordinary cyclicality. Price $173.05.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | 3.45% | 0.65 | Staffing enforcement / settlement forces the labor cost in; growth stalls | $33.53 | 4.95% |
| Bear | 25% | 10.45% | 0.90 | Q2 2026 cash-conversion stall sticks (OCF +10.4% vs revenue +17.3%); reimbursement barely covers labor inflation | $63.38 | 7.41% |
| Base | 30% | 17.45% | 1.00 | Guidance path: acquisitions + occupancy carry the fade | $95.99 | 9.98% |
| Bull | 20% | 20.45% | 1.10 | Acquisition pace and skilled-mix gains run above guidance | $120.48 | 11.71% |
